context: Year Up PACE long-term randomized outcome report; typed findings merged with the later approved sample repair.
name: Year Up randomly assigned 2,544 eligible young adults to program access or community alternatives in eight offices across nine cities.
description: The 2013–2014 PACE trial evaluated six months of IT/financial-services training followed by a six-month internship. It is one multi-site study, not independent evidence for each follow-up period.

values.value: Individual-level intent-to-treat randomized evaluation; 2,544 eligible applicants aged 18–24 with high-school credentials.

context: Year Up PACE long-term randomized outcome report; typed findings merged with the later approved sample repair.
name: Year Up increased average quarterly earnings in follow-up Quarters 23–24 by $1,895 (28%; $8,797 versus $6,901; SE $267; p < .001).
description: This was the report’s prespecified confirmatory earnings outcome, using National Directory of New Hires records. The $ figure is reported in the source’s earnings table; do not treat it as a common-price-year cost or a benefit-cost result.

values.value: USD difference in average quarterly National Directory of New Hires earnings in follow-up Quarters 23–24, program offer minus control.

context: Year Up PACE long-term randomized outcome report; typed findings merged with the later approved sample repair.
name: Year Up reduced total earnings in follow-up Year 1 by $5,778 ($3,964 versus $9,742; SE $259; p < .001).
description: The report attributes the early difference to treatment members prioritizing program participation over other work. It is part of the same seven-year earnings trajectory, not evidence from a separate trial.

values.value: USD difference in total National Directory of New Hires earnings in follow-up Year 1, program offer minus control.

context: Year Up PACE long-term randomized outcome report; typed findings merged with the later approved sample repair.
name: Year Up increased total earnings in follow-up Year 7 by $8,251 ($35,589 versus $27,338; SE $1,120; p < .001).
description: This is an intent-to-treat Year-7 earnings difference in the same NDNH sample. It should be read with the Year-1 displacement and cumulative seven-year result, not as an independent replication.

values.value: USD difference in total National Directory of New Hires earnings in follow-up Year 7, program offer minus control.

context: Year Up PACE long-term randomized outcome report; typed findings merged with the later approved sample repair.
name: Year Up increased total earnings over follow-up Years 1–7 by $38,152 ($176,412 versus $138,260; SE $3,958; p < .001).
description: This cumulative intent-to-treat earnings result spans the trial’s seven-year observation window. It does not establish lifetime earnings or the source’s separate cost-benefit model.

values.value: USD difference in total National Directory of New Hires earnings over follow-up Years 1–7, program offer minus control.

context: Year Up PACE long-term randomized outcome report; typed findings merged with the later approved sample repair.
name: Year Up increased the share earning at least $9,100 per quarter in Quarters 23–24 by 12.4 percentage points (44.1% versus 31.7%; SE 1.9; p < .001).
description: This is a secondary intent-to-treat earnings-threshold result in the NDNH sample. It is not an employment-rate effect.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in earning at least $9,100 per quarter in follow-up Quarters 23–24, program offer minus control.

context: Year Up PACE long-term randomized outcome report; typed findings merged with the later approved sample repair.
name: Year Up showed no impact on employment at the six-year follow-up.
description: The report says roughly 80% of both groups were working at the six-year survey and in Quarters 23–24. Higher earnings therefore should not be relabeled as a documented employment-rate gain.

values.value: Qualitative source finding: no employment-rate impact at six-year survey or follow-up Quarters 23–24.
